newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Gazprom cuts gas export to Belarus by half.
newsitem.headline: Russian Gazprom cuts gas export to Belarus by half.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly Gazprom has cut natural gas supplies to Belarus by 50 percent over delays in payments for the energy, a Gazprom spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We have cut gas supplies to Belarus by 50 percent," said Sergei Smirnov, adding the reduced volumes began last Saturday.
He said Belarussian gas company Beltransgaz owed Gazprom $125.5 million for supplies and that talks between the two to resolve the problem were due to be held in Moscow on Tuesday.
"We should be having talks with Belarus today. We are expecting Belarus' deputy prime minister (in charge of fuel and energy) Valery Kokorev to attend."

Interfax news agency quoted a Belarussian government source as saying pressure along Belarus' gas pipelines had dropped as a result of the supply cut, making it difficult to get Russian gas to Poland and Lithuania via Belarus.
But Smirnov said the supply cut to Belarus had had not no impact on the amount of gas to other countries.
Gazprom warned Belarus last week it would cut flows if they were not paid for.
Gazprom said in a statement on Tuesday it planned to supply 16.6 billion cubic metres (bcm) to Belarus in 1997. By mid-July 8.4 bcm worth $413.25 million has been sent.
Belarus had paid for $315.73 million of the total, and including penalties its overall debts to Gazprom were now $125.5 million, Smirnov said.

Gazprom signed an agreement with Beltransgaz in April on restructuring debts by paying $285 million in cash and an unspecified sum in supplies and services to Gazprom and Russian regions, the statement said.
"But the Belarussian side has failed to transfer the money regularly and provide the services. This was the reason for cutting gas supplies to Belarus," it said.
Moscow has in the past written off previous Belarussian gas debts in exchange for maintenance of Russian military sites and free transit of Russian gas to Poland.
